tooltip_why: Adding work makes your project bigger, and more expensive. All the work you take on together is your scope.
tooltip_context: Your scope decides how much money you need to raise.

tooltip_why: A bank lends you money that you pay back with interest. It is quicker and cheaper than an investor, but it lends less.
tooltip_context: Best for projects under $4 million.

tooltip_why: Investors can put in much more money than a bank, but they take longer to decide and cost more.
tooltip_context: Best for projects over $4 million.

tooltip_why: Life happens! Life Events represent unexpected developments that affect your project - sometimes good sometimes bad.
tooltip_context: Life Events add realism to project management. They can help or hurt your progress.

tooltip_why: A team member here is an expeditor: a specialist who knows how city approvals work. They can save you days or money later.
tooltip_context: Keep them for when they help most — your Expeditors box shows who you have.

tooltip_why: Trade one of your expeditors for a different one. Do it when the one you have will not help you soon.
tooltip_context: Each expeditor only helps in certain stages of the project. The new one is picked for you.

tooltip_why: One of your expeditors leaves your team, and the help they could give you leaves with them.
tooltip_context: Choose this only if you no longer need them.

tooltip_why: Sometimes you must share your resources with competitors. Choose wisely which expeditor to let go.
tooltip_context: Select your least useful expeditor to minimize the advantage you give to opponents.

tooltip_why: You hand one of your expeditors to the player next to you. They keep working for them, not for you.
tooltip_context: Optional. You need at least one to pass, and someone to pass it to.

tooltip_why: The owner decides how much work he wants done. This shows how much work is added to your project.
tooltip_context: More work means a bigger project, and more money to raise.

tooltip_why: This shows the deal the investors offer: how much they put in.
tooltip_context: They may take longer and charge more than a bank.

tooltip_why: This shows whether you get a new team member — an expeditor — from this step.
tooltip_context: Your Expeditors box shows who you have.

tooltip_why: This shows what you pay for this step. Fees are a share of your project's cost, so a bigger project pays more.
A contractor's crew can be top, average, or budget quality. Better crews cost about 15% more but build faster; budget crews save money but slow the job.
tooltip_context: This sets both your price and your schedule.

tooltip_why: The contractor's bid sets the price you agree to and how long the job takes. A higher bid means a higher price and a longer job.
tooltip_context: The price lands between about 80% and 130% of your estimate; crew quality shifts both.

tooltip_why: Two things get decided here: how good the crew is, and the price and schedule they bid.
tooltip_context: Better crews cost more up front but finish sooner.

tooltip_why: Some steps take longer than you planned for. This shows how many days this step costs you.
tooltip_context: Days you spend count against your final score.

tooltip_why: Your path forward depends on approvals inspections and reviews. The dice determine which department you visit next.
tooltip_context: Building projects require multiple agency approvals. Each roll may send you forward or back.

tooltip_why: Change orders extend timelines and add costs. The dice determine the impact of modifications.
tooltip_context: Subsequent CON-INITIATION visits represent changes. Time and cost increases vary.

tooltip_why: Movement dice determine your next destination. Your roll will reveal the available paths forward.
tooltip_context: Some spaces have fixed destinations. Others depend on your roll result.

tooltip_why: You have completed all required actions for this turn. End your turn to let the next player proceed.
tooltip_context: All mandatory effects have been resolved. Press to advance the game.

tooltip_why: Unhappy with your outcome? Negotiate to try again next turn - but it costs an extra turn.
tooltip_context: Some spaces allow negotiation. Consider if waiting is worth a potentially better result.

tooltip_why: Project fees are due! These costs come from your available funds and go toward permits approvals and professional services.
tooltip_context: Fees are automatically deducted based on space requirements and dice rolls.

tooltip_why: Reviewing scope may result in changes. Your roll determines if work is added removed replaced or unchanged.
tooltip_context: Design reviews can modify your Work Packages. Be prepared for scope creep or reductions.

tooltip_why: Return to project management for reassessment. Use this when you need to reconsider your project direction.
tooltip_context: PM Decision lets you evaluate progress and choose next steps strategically.

tooltip_why: Visit the lender to negotiate scope changes tied to funding requirements.
tooltip_context: Lenders may require scope adjustments in exchange for better loan terms.

tooltip_why: Apply for bank financing. Banks offer smaller loans quickly at lower interest rates.
tooltip_context: Best for projects under $4M. Faster approval but limited funding amounts.

tooltip_why: Seek investor funding. Investors provide larger amounts but take longer and charge higher rates.
tooltip_context: Best for projects over $4M. More capital but higher cost and longer wait.

tooltip_why: Begin or continue architectural design phase. The architect creates your project drawings.
tooltip_context: Required before engineering. Architect sets the design direction.

tooltip_why: Negotiate architect compensation. Design fees are a percentage of project scope.
tooltip_context: First visit: 8-12% of scope. Subsequent visits: 0-2% for revisions.

tooltip_why: Review architectural scope. The design may need changes based on the review outcome.
tooltip_context: Roll determines if Work Packages are added removed replaced or unchanged.

tooltip_why: Begin or continue engineering design phase. Engineers handle structural and systems design.
tooltip_context: Required after architecture. Engineering makes the design buildable.

tooltip_why: Negotiate engineer compensation. Engineering fees are a percentage of project scope.
tooltip_context: First visit: 2-6% of scope. Subsequent visits: 0-2% for revisions.

tooltip_why: Review engineering scope. Technical requirements may change the project.
tooltip_context: Roll determines if Work Packages are added removed replaced or unchanged.

tooltip_why: Present options to the project owner for their decision on scope and direction.
tooltip_context: Owners have final say. Their decisions affect both Work Packages and Expeditors.

tooltip_why: Attempt to bypass normal approval processes. Risky but potentially time-saving.
tooltip_context: High risk high reward. Bad rolls can add months to your project.

tooltip_why: Pay Department of Buildings filing fees. Required before plan review or permits.
tooltip_context: DOB fees are 1% of scope. Required for all permit applications.

tooltip_why: Select your permit approval method: Plan Exam (slow safe) or Prof Cert (fast risky).
tooltip_context: Plan Exam: DOB reviews everything. Prof Cert: Your architect certifies but faces audit risk.

tooltip_why: Submit to DOB Plan Examination. Thorough review takes time but reduces rejection risk.
tooltip_context: Safer path but slower. Examiner reviews all code compliance.

tooltip_why: Use Professional Certification. Your architect certifies compliance risking audit.
tooltip_context: Faster path but risky. If audited and failed you go back to Plan Exam.

tooltip_why: Your professionally certified application is being audited for code compliance.
tooltip_context: Audit can pass you through or send you back to Plan Exam or design.

tooltip_why: Final DOB inspection before project completion. Last hurdle before Certificate of Occupancy.
tooltip_context: Almost done! Pass this and you reach the finish line.

tooltip_why: Pay Fire Department fees for fire safety review and permits.
tooltip_context: FDNY fees are 1% of scope. Required for fire safety compliance.

tooltip_why: Submit to Fire Department plan examination for fire safety compliance.
tooltip_context: FDNY reviews sprinklers alarms exits and fire safety systems.

tooltip_why: Hire a contractor or negotiate change orders. Construction finally begins or changes.
tooltip_context: First visit: Select contractor quality. Later visits: Handle change orders.

tooltip_why: Address problems discovered during construction. Issues may require redesign or re-permitting.
tooltip_context: Construction reveals hidden conditions. May need to revisit design or permits.

tooltip_why: Construction inspection by DOB inspector. Pass to move forward fail to address issues.
tooltip_context: Inspectors verify work matches approved plans. Critical checkpoint.

tooltip_why: Congratulations! Your project is complete. Calculate your final score.
tooltip_context: All approvals obtained. Compare completion time and remaining funds to win.
